derived.name: Driver score
derived.rule: The mean of its scored questions' scores (0 to 100). An N/A answer is left out.

derived.name: Explorer score
derived.rule: The mean of its scored questions' scores (I2). An N/A answer is left out. Shown separately and unscored questions never count.

derived.name: SHAPE score (overall)
derived.rule: The mean of the 12 Explorer scores, so each Explorer counts equally. The mean is confirmed (I2); averaging Explorers rather than every question is the choice made for now.

derived.name: Question level breakdown (QLB)
derived.rule: Not a score: a chart of an Explorer broken down question by question (I2).

derived.name: Status
derived.rule: Struggling 0 to 59, Striving 60 to 79, Flourishing 80 to 100 (the product's scale, lib/bands.js).

derived.name: Work model
derived.rule: Office if every contracted hour is at the office, Home if every hour is at home, Hybrid if both (I16). Not asked directly.
derived.from: Your Profile Q12 (office and home hours)

derived.name: Age
derived.rule: Years since the date of birth, on the day the round closes.

derived.name: eNPS
derived.rule: Promoters answer 9 or 10, Passives 7 or 8, Detractors 0 to 6. eNPS = % Promoters − % Detractors (−100 to 100). Only from Corporate Culture 2.3 (I20); it also counts in Corporate Culture as a 0 to 100 score.

derived.name: Mental well-being
derived.rule: Three measures from the nine DASS questions (the short form is intentional, I21): Feeling Low = Depression (PSY1.2, PSY1.6, PSY1.8); Feeling Stressed = Stress (PSY1.1, PSY1.3, PSY1.5); Feeling Anxious = Anxiety (PSY1.4, PSY1.7, PSY1.9). Each falls into one of five levels: Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Extremely Severe.

derived.name: Mental well-being levels
derived.rule: On each measure's 0 to 100 score (100 = Never): Normal 80+, Mild 60 to 79, Moderate 40 to 59, Severe 20 to 39, Extremely Severe under 20. The product's current assumption; the real cut-offs for the 9-item form are still to come (I22).

derived.name: HPQ performance
derived.rule: Standard HPQ scoring: absolute performance = Q16.3 × 10 (0 to 100); relative performance = Q16.3 ÷ Q16.1. Never part of the SHAPE score; Time & Money reads it.

derived.name: Work environment for Hybrid people
derived.rule: Asked twice for Hybrid people, once for the office and once for home. The two answers are averaged, weighted by their contracted office and home hours (Your Profile Q12). For now (I14).
derived.from: PhysWE1.1-1.8, SoftWE1.1-1.6 and Your Profile Q12

issues.title: Two Explorer names differ between sheets
issues.detail: The survey says Life Outside Work and Business Essentials; ScoredNonscored says Factors Outside Work and Business Fundamentals.
issues.answer: Life Outside Work and Business Essentials are the right names.

issues.title: How scores are calculated isn't in the file
issues.detail: The file says which questions are scored and what each answer is worth, but not how they're combined. ScoredNonscored also mentions a “QLB calculation”.
issues.answer: The mean, for now. QLB is the question level breakdown: a chart of an Explorer question by question, not a calculation. Averaging Explorers (not every question) for the overall score is the choice made for now.

issues.title: Life Outside Work Q1: the strain scale doesn't match
issues.detail: The survey offers Severe / High / Moderate / Low / No strain and N/A. The scoring sheet scores A lot / A moderate amount / A little / Not at all.
issues.answer: Use the five strain levels: Severe 0, High 25, Moderate 50, Low 75, No strain 100. N/A is left out.

issues.title: Life Outside Work Q3 (support network): the scale doesn't match
issues.detail: The survey asks for agreement; the scoring sheet scores Non-existent / Minimal / Sufficient / Extensive.
issues.answer: Agreement (Strongly agree to Strongly disagree) is correct.

issues.title: Coworker Dynamic has no scoring scale
issues.detail: All 12 questions are scored, but the scoring sheet has no values for All / Most / About half / Some / None.
issues.answer: All 100, Most 75, About half 50, Some 25, None 0.

issues.title: Situational Leadership has no formula
issues.detail: Manager Style Q1 (how often the manager uses each of four styles) and Q2.1 (your competence) are scored, and Q1.1's Driver is Situational Leadership. The file has no formula; its “SR1.1, 1.3, 1.5 (MS)” scale matches no question.
issues.answer: There may be discrepancies; how it's scored is to come.
issues.proposal: Until then the five questions are grouped as Situational Leadership with no score. A likely formula: match the style the person's competence calls for (Low → Directive, Moderate → Coaching, High → Supporting, Very high → Delegating) and score how often the manager uses it.

issues.title: Manager Style numbering is out of date in the scoring sheets
issues.detail: The scoring sheet's MS2.4 (Very effective … Poor) is now Q2.6. Role clarity (2.4) and Manager cares (2.5) were added later.
issues.answer: The scoring sheet is out of date here: its 2.4 is the survey's 2.6. Scored: 1, 2.1-2.4 and 2.6; 2.5 shown separately.

issues.title: Smoking: “Ex Smoker” has no score
issues.detail: The survey offers Ex Smoker; the scoring sheet doesn't score it.
issues.answer: Keep it 100 for now; to be clarified.

issues.title: BMI scores underweight as the best band
issues.detail: Under 24 scores 100, so a BMI of 16 scores the same as 22.
issues.answer: A real finding: the team is discussing it. Kept as the file has it for now.

issues.title: Soft Work Environment 1.7 is in both lists
issues.detail: Scored range says 1.1-1.7; the non-scored list has 1.7. It's a free-text question.
issues.answer: Free text is never scored.

issues.title: The agreement scale's list names questions that don't exist
issues.answer: Out of date. EE1.1-1.9 and JS2.1-2.5 are correct. PWE was an old Explorer (Personal Work Ethic) that has been removed.

issues.title: A reverse-worded statement
issues.detail: “I suffer from physical and/or mental health issues as a result of stress”: agreeing is the bad answer.
issues.answer: Don't reverse it: it isn't scored.

issues.title: Job Satisfaction 1.2 (demands) has no clear direction
issues.detail: “How would you rate the demands of your job?” 1 to 5: is a high number good or bad?
issues.answer: Job Satisfaction Q1 is shown as smileys: 5 is the biggest smile, so 5 is good.

issues.title: Work environment questions asked twice for Hybrid people
issues.detail: “Asked from WFO + WFH perspective separately given the user's status.” How the two answers combine wasn't stated.
issues.answer: Weight the office and home answers by the contracted office and home hours (Your Profile Q12). A better answer may follow.

issues.title: Lists not in the file
issues.detail: Country (“all countries with a few exceptions”), ethnicity (depends on country), site codes (set per client) and annual salary (“separate algorithm”) have no options in the file.
issues.answer: A full country list for now; the annual salary bands depend on the country picked. The exceptions, the ethnicity lists and the salary bands are still to come.

issues.title: Work model isn't asked directly
issues.detail: The survey asks contracted hours at the office and at home, not a work model.
issues.answer: All office hours = Office, all home hours = Home, both = Hybrid. The product's “Onsite” and “Remote” labels become Office and Home.

issues.title: Driver names that collide
issues.detail: “Coworker Dynamic” is both an Explorer and a Driver inside Employee Engagement. (Flexible / Flexibility and Policies / Policies and Practices are also pairs, but they're different things and stay as they are.)
issues.answer: Rename the Employee Engagement Driver. It's now “Working relationships”.

issues.title: Scored questions without a Driver
issues.detail: Some scored questions count towards their Explorer but name no Driver.
issues.answer: Each is its own Driver, named by its short label. (Manager Style 1.2-1.4 and 2.1 have no short label: they're grouped under Situational Leadership, I6.)

issues.title: Small fixes in the text
issues.detail: “consistant” (hover label, Soft Work Environment 1.6). “*manager x*” is a placeholder for the manager's name.
issues.answer: Fixed: “consistent”, and the placeholder is now a {manager's name} slot. The file's text is kept beside each.

issues.title: eNPS: three wordings on the eNPS sheet
issues.detail: The eNPS sheet offers a list version and 1-10 or 0-10 versions.
issues.answer: eNPS comes from Corporate Culture 2.3 only, the standard 0 to 10 question.

issues.title: Psychological Health uses 9 DASS questions
issues.detail: Three each for stress, depression and anxiety (the full DASS-21 has seven each).
issues.answer: Intentional. They feed the Mental Well-Being widgets: Depression → Feeling Low, Stress → Feeling Stressed, Anxiety → Feeling Anxious, each in five levels (Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Extremely Severe).

issues.title: Mental well-being level cut-offs
issues.detail: The five levels are confirmed, but not where one ends and the next begins for this 9-question form.
issues.proposal: On each measure's 0 to 100 score: Normal 80+, Mild 60 to 79, Moderate 40 to 59, Severe 20 to 39, Extremely Severe under 20 (the product's current assumption).
